clue.text: Gum with which Alice got involved

definitions.text: Gum with which Alice got involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved become entangled with one another, so the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A child named Alice ends up stuck in some chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of GUM entangled with ALICE make a gummy substance. 'got involved' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucilage is a viscous plant secretion used as an adhesive, a kind of gum, and here the gum is formed from the mingled words.

clue.text: American doctor, bellicose type

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a hawk is someone who favours war

explanation.surface: An American doctor turns out to be a warmonger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' is the definition, a Native American people, not a modifier of 'doctor'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are one of the Native peoples of North America, part of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Church partners or Roman official

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: Choosing between church partners and an official in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the censor was a magistrate who kept the citizen register and oversaw public morals.

clue.text: Continuing gravity amid the lack of it is characteristic of the turtle

indicators.note: the letters go in the middle of another word

parts.note: levity is the lack of gravity, meaning frivolousness
on means continuing, as in carry on
G is the symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A remark that the tortoise-like turtle has gravity rather than frivolity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to gravity, so 'the lack of it' is LEVITY, the opposite of seriousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Turtles are famous for living a very long time, so long life is their characteristic.

clue.text: Wins urban seat in 11

parts.note: gains are wins or acquisitions
a borough was a town returning a member to Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone wins a town constituency in a county.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 is Lincolnshire, an English county in the east Midlands; the town is also the name of the painter of 'The Blue Boy', which 6-down needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough is a market town in Lincolnshire, on the River Trent.

clue.text: Sailor to take no action on fire

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
to laze is to idle and do nothing

explanation.surface: A lazy sailor refuses to act even when something is burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burning fiercely is described as aflame, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Music for 4's boy and 2's 20

definitions.meaning: a genre of melancholy song from the American South
Gainsborough's painting is The Blue Boy and the censor's instrument is the blue pencil, so both take this colour

explanation.surface: Some music played for a painter's son and an official's writing tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Gainsborough painted 'The Blue Boy', and a censor wields the blue pencil, so the colour serves both cross-references.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues is a style of music, and the plural colour word also covers both the boy and the pencil.

clue.text: Nearly a lot of money, a 12 to stomach

indicators.note: almost all of the phrase is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a bomb is slang for a large sum of money
the answer to 12-across, a whole, is a sum

explanation.surface: Almost a fortune, a whole sum, goes to someone's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts A BOMB to ABOM; 12-across's answer (complete) gives SUM, as in a total.
explanation.definitionFit: The abomasum is the fourth compartment of a ruminant's digestive system, the true stomach of a cow.

clue.text: Serious request for directions by agreement

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
a treaty is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: Someone earnestly asks for directions as part of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, a heartfelt appeal for something.

clue.text: "Ghana — 0" result of finger problem

indicators.note: the answer is what comes out of working on the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the figure zero is nil, as in a football score

explanation.surface: A football scoreline in which Ghana fail to score.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a match result with Ghana on nil; 'result of' says GHANA plus NIL are reworked into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangnail is a torn strip of skin beside a fingernail, a common minor complaint of the finger.

clue.text: Marine beast mostly taking note in trench

indicators.note: only most of the sea creature's name is kept, its tail being cut off

parts.note: the dugong is a sea mammal related to the manatee
UT is the old name for the note now called doh

explanation.surface: A sea creature digs itself into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last two letters NG from DUGONG, leaving DUGO, which takes the note UT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a shelter dug into the ground, a trench used by soldiers.

clue.text: Hundreds into riding here and briefly golf, say

definitions.meaning: the ridings of this county were subdivided into hundreds or wapentakes
the county's short form Lincs sounds the same as links, a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: Somewhere hundreds go riding and there is a quick round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: This English county's ridings (the three parts of Lindsey) split into smaller units called hundreds; its abbreviation, Lincs, is spoken like 'links'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincolnshire is an English county once divided into ridings and hundreds, abbreviated Lincs.

clue.text: Complete with gap

parts.note: a hole is an opening or gap

explanation.surface: Something is called complete even though it has a gap in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and complete are synonyms, both meaning entire with nothing missing.

clue.text: Tapering forwards and downwards, and blunt at the back, which is neat

definitions.text: Tapering forwards and downwards, and blunt at the back
definitions.meaning: a playful description of the outline of a vessel's hull: pointed at the bow, rounded below, square at the stern

explanation.surface: A description of some object's tapering outline, concluding that it looks tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape is an idiom meaning tidy and orderly, and literally it is the form of a ship.

clue.text: Here splits and twists reoccur, splitting piece of turf

indicators.note: one piece breaks the other open by sitting inside it

parts.note: a divot is a chunk of turf cut out, as by a golf swing

indicators.note: the word is twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere couples split up and the same twists keep recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' looks like a verb but means marital break-ups; the definition 'Here splits' names the place where they happen. 'twists' rearranges the fodder and 'splitting' puts it inside the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorce court is where marriages are legally dissolved, the place where couples go through a split.

clue.text: Force painter to study horses?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a stable is a group of horses kept together

explanation.surface: A painter is forced to study horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: a member of the police force, and John Constable, the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer, a member of the force, and Constable is a famous English painter.

clue.text: Moorland dweller's temperature during erosion

indicators.note: one thing happens within another, so its letters sit inside

parts.note: wear is gradual erosion
heat is a measure of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone living on the moors notes how temperature affects erosion.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird that breeds on open upland moors.

clue.text: Friend to Picasso with no love for your leader, as you can see

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: the item named is taken away from the name

parts.note: Pablo was the first name of the painter Picasso
love means nil, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friend writes to Picasso, without affection, telling him to look for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes O (love, zero in tennis) from PABLO; 'leader' picks the first letter of 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpably means obviously or evidently, so plainly that it can be perceived.

clue.text: Many votes cast, very weird ploy during therapy

indicators.note: one thing happens within another, so one set of letters goes inside the other

parts.note: healing is a form of therapy

indicators.note: something weird is odd and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange political ploy carried out during treatment leads to a big turnout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' signals the rearrangement and 'during' the insertion; 'cast' belongs to the definition, as votes are cast, rather than suggesting an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy polling describes an election with a high turnout, many ballots being cast.

clue.text: Sugar donned as home to the 11

definitions.meaning: fine white sugar used for baking
given DON in front, this becomes Doncaster, where the Lincoln Handicap horse race is now run

explanation.surface: Some sugar is put on, at the home of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lincoln Handicap (here 'the 11') moved to Doncaster racecourse in 1965, so putting DON before this word gives its home.
explanation.definitionFit: Caster sugar is a finely ground white sugar used in baking, often just called caster.

clue.text: Line 15 might take with writer

definitions.meaning: a painter such as Constable sketches a line with this drawing tool

explanation.surface: A painter might draw a line with a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a writing and drawing instrument, which an artist uses to draw lines.

clue.text: Snake with backing of sugar, a delicacy

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the following words are read from back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake comes with sugar on it, served as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' turns 'sugar, a' round to give ARAGUS after ASP.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus spears are a prized seasonal vegetable often regarded as a gourmet treat.

clue.text: Right old city with others not citified

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city
al from et al, Latin for and others

explanation.surface: A rightful ancient city with others remains countrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside, the opposite of urban or city life.

clue.text: A little bit of horse?

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, a hint of something
a strap of harness by which a horse pulls a cart

explanation.surface: A question about a small piece of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is both a tiny amount and one of the side straps attaching a draught animal to its load.

clue.text: Setter backing his word "Begin!"

indicators.note: the setter's self-reference is turned back to front

parts.note: the setter of the puzzle refers to themself as me
a dog such as a setter says woof, its bark

explanation.surface: A crossword setter backs up his order to get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' plays two parts: as the compiler it gives ME, turned round by 'backing'; as a dog breed, its word is a bark.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to start or set out on something, so it serves as a command to begin.

clue.text: Princess to assist (with a lot of diamonds) one with sugar problem

parts.note: DI recalls Diana, Princess of Wales
to abet is to help

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is kept, its last letter being dropped

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A princess helps out, wearing plenty of diamonds, to aid someone with a blood-sugar condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ICE (slang for diamonds) to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabetic person has a condition in which the body cannot regulate blood glucose properly.

clue.text: Top people with the 6

definitions.meaning: members of the monarch's family are society's highest
the Blues and ... is a cavalry regiment of the Household Cavalry, so this word goes with 6-down

explanation.surface: Elite people come in company with some music.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blues and Royals is a British Army cavalry regiment, so this word partners 6-down's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a royal family are informally called this, being people at the very top of society.

clue.text: Apply wax to support student that's brainy

parts.note: to cere is to wrap or coat in wax
a bra is a supporting undergarment
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A clever student waxes a piece of support.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means intellectual, appealing to the mind rather than feelings.
